facts.value: Good architecture improves ordinary life. It can make a home easier to live in, a school easier to learn in, a park more welcoming, and a workplace less draining. Light, air, circulation, layout, and proportion all affect how a place feels long before anyone starts talking about style.
Buildings carry memory. They reflect local values, climate, technology, religion, politics, and available materials.
Architecture affects value. Strong civic buildings, well-designed streets, and memorable landmarks can attract visitors, investment, and long-term reuse.
Buildings consume huge amounts of energy and materials, making architecture one of the most important fields for reducing waste, improving building performance, and responding better to climate.

A design is not fully tested when it is drawn. It is tested years later when buildings settle, materials move, sealants fail, finishes fade, drainage issues show up, and the gap between a beautiful rendering and a durable building becomes obvious.
Doors start sticking, floors slope slightly, sun damage shows up on one side first, water finds small mistakes and makes them expensive, and people use rooms differently than the plan expected.
